patch_description:
Replace selected two-hop rewards with a two-facility routing model. Each possible pair of outgoing links is evaluated jointly: traffic is split between the two branches using multiscale diffusion distances and a congestion-balancing cost. The transposed calculation evaluates incoming-link pairs.

These pair costs are decomposed into linear link preferences and centered quadratic interactions. Only the strongest interactions are retained, with a mean-field correction for sparsification. A small reciprocal-link cost discourages wasted local circulation. This targets complementary branches and balanced traffic distribution rather than repeatedly rewarding overlapping paths; its diffusion horizon also grows with network size. Performance improvements require evaluation rather than being guaranteed.
